Subject: Post-demo: batching & concurrency — unit economics and workload patterns

Hi Samir / Alicia —

Great to meet this morning. Quick recap / next steps so we’re aligned on what a pricing + PoC conversation would need: 

Key points from today’s demo:
- Workload mix: synchronous chat (user-facing, latency-sensitive) + continuous personalization scoring (background, lower latency SLOs).
- Current reported baseline: ~80M tokens / month now, goal to scale to ~250–400M tokens / month over the next 12 months (Samir, correct me if I’m off).
- Peak concurrency: you mentioned spikes to ~220 concurrent requests in morning windows, steady-state background scoring at ~8–12 qps.
- Continuous batching assumption: you expect our runtime to maintain a rolling batching window (continuous KV cache + background batching) rather than discrete bulk-batch jobs.

What we need from you to finalize an indicative quote and PoC scope:
1) Confirm a 3-band monthly volume estimate (low/expected/high) and any committed baseline you’re comfortable with.
2) Share a small sample of traffic characteristics (CSV of per-request median tokens + timestamp for ~48–72 hours).
3) Callouts on latency SLOs for chat vs. scoring (e.g., 200ms p95 for chat).

Draft commercial thinking (indicative):
- Target unit-econ the call surfaced: ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens for chat model w/ baseline quantization + continuous batching at expected concurrency.
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost materially compared to always-spot single-request execution — see attached assumptions workbook for a quick sensitivity table.

Next steps (proposed):
- You send a short sample export and the monthly volume banding by EOD Thu (9/2).
- We schedule a technical PoC kickoff (1hr) next week to validate latency under continuous-batching and to agree on logging/metric collection.
- I’ll follow up with an indicative quote and a proposed commit/discount band once we have the sample traffic.

Attachments: 20260830-batching-assumptions.xlsx (assumptions & sensitivity), redwood-indicative-quote.pdf (placeholder).

Thanks —
Laura Bennett

Thanks for the quick numbers and the sample, Samir — that helps a lot. A few quick notes from our side (internal calc + immediate answers):

Cold-starts & continuous batching:
- Cold windows (multi-hour idle) do increase per-token overhead because GPUs need to re-warm KV caches and micro-batching ramps. In practice we see an incremental per-token penalty concentrated in the first 3–10 minutes of a warm-up spike. For your pattern (spike to ~220 conc after quiet overnight), we estimate an extra ~6–12% per-token cost on that spike segment versus steady-state.

Indicative unit-econ buckets (very high level):
- Chat (latency-sensitive, p95 ~250ms): ~$950 / 1M tokens (standard quantized model, continuous batching tuned).
- Background scoring (lower SLO): ~$500 / 1M tokens with the same commitments — here batching can amortize KV and significantly reduce CPU/GPU idle cycles.

Commit sensitivity: with a 12-month committed baseline in the expected band (300M/mo) we can comfortably move chat pricing to ~$820 / 1M and scoring to ~$420 / 1M — I’ve put those bands into the attached worksheet.

Immediate ask from our side: Sean / Monica — can either of you confirm whether we want to propose a single blended $/1M for the whole account or keep separate chat vs. scoring buckets? Also advise on one-time PoC discount (15% recommended) to accelerate the kickoff.

Samir / Alicia: I’ll book the PoC kickoff for next Tue unless you prefer another slot — the agenda will be load profile replay, latency measurements under continuous batching, and logging/metric plan.

Thanks,
Laura

Based on the spike shape, continuous batching should capture ~18–22% savings in steady-state per-token relative to single-request execution; the warm-up window adds headroom as Laura noted.

2) Given Vectra’s target ranges, recommended commercial approach:
- Keep separate SKUs: Chat SKU (latency SLO-backed) and Scoring SKU (background).
- Indicative list: Chat $950/1M, Scoring $500/1M.
- If Vectra signs a 12-month 300M/mo baseline commit we can offer Chat $820/1M, Scoring $420/1M + a one-time 15% PoC credit.

3) PoC ask list (to scope infra & measurement):
- 72-hour request-level export (timestamps + token counts) — you already shared a good slice, want one more weekend sample.
- Access to a staging key for replay (time-limited) + expected concurrency targets per minute.
- A short integration doc specifying any custom preprocessing (we’ll replicate exactly).

I’ll prepare a short, two-sheet quote that separates list vs. committed pricing and includes a sensitivity for warm-up overhead. Laura — if OK I’ll share the quote PDF to Samir/Alicia this afternoon.
